description: Hello all! Today's festivities feature a slightly restless Microsoft tech support "manager" calling me after I trolled his scam call center for over 3 hours. Enjoy! Follow me: Patreon :play button: https://www.patreon.com/TheHoaxHotel Twitter :play button: https://twitter.com/thehoaxhotel Facebook :play button: https://www.facebook.com/TheHoaxHotel Instagram :play button: https://instagram.com/thehoaxhotel/  This is the classic "Microsoft" Tech Support scam, and these technicians claiming to be from Windows will tell you that your computer has these "viruses" that send error reports to their special servers somehow. Scare tactic BS. The scammers attempt to remote connect to your computer through various legitimate programs on sites such as Ammyy.com, Teamviewer.com, and logmein and others. The scammers then attempt to charge you ridiculous amounts of money for their "help." Huge scam and absolute BS. Have fun listening to this call! He gets a little pissed... Number is down and hasn't worked in months. If I find him again, you're the first to know.  Had a lot of fun with this call. textual.observation: The description reports a purported Microsoft/Windows tech-support scheme in which callers claim a computer has viruses, seek remote access through software, and then attempt to charge for assistance.

evidence.quote: This is the classic "Microsoft" Tech Support scam, and these technicians claiming to be from Windows will tell you that your computer has these "viruses" that send error reports to their special servers somehow.

The scammers attempt to remote connect to your computer through various legitimate programs on sites such as Ammyy.com, Teamviewer.com, and logmein and others. The scammers then attempt to charge you ridiculous amounts of money for their "help."

textual.context: The source presents this as a warning/reporting and trolling call rather than an offer by the video creator; the description explicitly labels the conduct a scam. The caller's statements in the ASR are part of a recorded conversation, and endorsement by the caller is unclear.

textual.limitations: These records do not independently establish the callers' identity, whether remote access or payment actually occurred, or whether every ASR statement is accurately transcribed.

annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary context is warning, criticizing and testing a purported third-party tech-support scam: the description identifies a trolling call, reports the alleged false-virus and remote-access mechanism, and the dialogue challenges the caller's claims.

evidence.observation: The description frames the video as a trolling interaction with a purported scam call center.
evidence.quote: Today's festivities feature a slightly restless Microsoft tech support "manager" calling me after I trolled his scam call center for over 3 hours.

evidence.observation: The description reports a purported support identity making false-virus claims.
evidence.quote: This is the classic "Microsoft" Tech Support scam, and these technicians claiming to be from Windows will tell you that your computer has these "viruses" that send error reports to their special servers somehow.

evidence.observation: The description reports a purported support scheme linking remote computer access with attempted charges for assistance.
evidence.quote: The scammers attempt to remote connect to your computer through various legitimate programs on sites such as Ammyy.com, Teamviewer.com, and logmein and others. The scammers then attempt to charge you ridiculous amounts of money for their "help."

evidence.observation: In the recorded dialogue, one speaker attributes fake-virus claims, computer connection and attempts to obtain payment to the other party.
evidence.quote: You say there's fake viruses on computers that compromises the system. And then you connect to the computers and try and get people to pay the money.

evidence.observation: A speaker describes the purported caller's virus-and-repair claim as false.
evidence.quote: You call and say that people like that. You say people have viruses on their computers and that you can fix it, but you know that's a lie.

evidence.observation: The purported caller makes a Microsoft-certified-technician affiliation claim while denying that the company is Microsoft.
evidence.quote: I never said that we are Microsoft. I said we are Microsoft certified technician.

evidence.observation: The recorded interaction is confrontational and explicitly challenges the purported caller about being a scam.
evidence.quote: Just admit that you're a scam and this will all be over.

evidence.observation: The supplied frame shows an animated headset-wearing character beside a sign reading "MIKRUSOFT SUPPORT, LLC." with a subtitle stating, "I'm calling you be- on behalf my company."
The supplied frame shows the animated support character with a subtitle referring to connecting "the computer with the customer's computer."
The supplied frame shows an animated character marked "FBI" with a subtitle stating, "I have your aa-aah address in the information, do."
